subject: QBR prep: capacity planning + unit economics (GPU spend, utilization, batching)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: capacity planning + unit economics (GPU spend, utilization, batching)

Team — starting the QBR slide set for infra & unit economics. Attached is the current capacity model (qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx). We need to lock a few numbers by Wednesday so the exec slides can include:

- 6–12 month capacity plan (GPU count by family)
- expected 99th/median latency targets that we will present vs. target SLOs
- baseline GPU-hour cost and assumed utilization on Dedicated and Hosted
- material impact of batching / prefix caching on per-token unit cost (we want a defensible % reduction)

Action items for each of you: please reply with the two-page summary we can drop into the slide: (1) top-line projection + key assumptions, (2) biggest risk/ask. If you have simulation outputs, attach them.

Notes: we expect a potential Dedicated ramp from one enterprise in EU in Q4 (still NDA) — assume conservative 40% capacity reservation unless you think otherwise.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity planning + unit economics (GPU spend, utilization, batching)

Hannah — attached a concise summary and the quick sim outputs (batching-sim-results.pdf). Top-line:

- Baseline assumptions: p3d-equivalent hourly cost $3.40 (hosted blended), utilization baseline 48% across multi-tenant hosted fleet, Dedicated pools assumed 65% util when committed.
- Unit economics (current): ~$0.0026 per token (median mix) on hosted; Dedicated reduces token cost by ~28% at projected utils.
- Batching + KV-prefix caching: our sim shows batching (target batch size 12 avg) + 20% prefix hit-rate -> combined 18–22% reduction in per-token GPU time. If we tune cache TTLs for session-based workloads, expected hit-rate could reach 35% for some products -> ~30% unit reduction.

Biggest risks / asks:
- We cannot safely target >70% long-term utilization without more aggressive autoscaling granularity; that raises latency tail risk. Recommend we present a target utilisation band (65% committed / 45–55% hosted).
- Need decision on whether to push quantized variants into Hosted canary (saves ~12% token cost) — that affects capacity planning.

Attaching sim PDF and a 1-page slide export.

—Marcus
Senior Capacity Planner
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-ai.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity planning + unit economics (GPU spend, utilization, batching)

Adding Optimize team notes — pulled from live traces this morning. Key points:

- Workload mix: ~62% short-chat (<=256 tokens), 28% mid (256–1024), 10% long (>1024). Short-chat workloads benefit most from prefix caching & KV reuse.
- Recommendation: enable session-level prefix caching + 200s TTL for chat flows. Estimated immediate win: +12–18% token savings on chat-dominant routes.
- Batching: continuous batching gives good amortization but we see diminishing returns beyond mean batch ~14 due to increased 99th latency. Sweet spot: 9–12.

Attachment: optimize_caching_notes.docx (contains per-route expected hit-rates and conservative/worst-case scenarios).

Risk/ask: if we surface a >20% unit-cost improvement in the slide, we should include the conservative lower-bound (10%) and a sensitivity table. Ops partners (Acme) asked to review our assumptions — CC'd their ops contact.

Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Optimize
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity planning + unit economics (GPU spend, utilization, batching)

Thanks — collating into the QBR deck. Quick summary I will use unless you push back:

- Present committed vs hosted: committed util target 65% (baseline), hosted util band 45–55%.
- Baseline per-token cost: $0.0026 (hosted blended), with conservative caching/batching upside of 10% and optimistic upside of 30% (include sensitivity table).
- Capacity ask: +120 p3d-equivalent GPUs over next 6 months (50% Dedicated, 50% Hosted burstable). This shows headroom for the EU enterprise commitment at 40% reservation.

Question for Hannah: are we comfortable with including quantized-variant plan as a line item (12% saving) or should that be an appendix note?

Dylan

Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity planning + unit economics (GPU spend, utilization, batching)

Thanks everyone — this is exactly what I needed. Decisions / next steps:

- Accept Dylan's summary for the exec slide. Put quantized-variant plan in Appendix B (callout: expected ~12% additional reduction; will require canary before presenting as baseline).
- Use conservative caching uplift of 10% on the main slide and include optimistic 30% in sensitivity. Marcus, please include the 65%/45–55% util bands on slide 3.
- Commit to ordering the +120 p3d-equivalent capacity (50/50 split). Finance sign-off flagged; I will escalate tomorrow morning — please pull precise CAPEX/OPEX numbers from the spreadsheet.
- Schedule: finalize deck by Wednesday 10:00 PT. 30-minute sync at 09:30 PT to run through slides. Calendar invite incoming.

Attachments to include in deck: qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx, batching-sim-results.pdf (summary page).
